To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the interconnection and damping passivity-based control method can be successfully applied to power system control problems; (2) a well-defined estimate on the domain of attraction can be obtained by means of a Lyapunov-like function; (3) the control design procedure requires the introduction of state-dependent interconnections that play a crucial role in the stabilization process; (4) the closed-loop system has an energy function with a physical interpretation; (5) the proposed control scheme is robust

the interconnection and damping passivity-based control design methodology, originally developed in the context of mechanical systems with nonnegatively defined energy functions, can be extended to systems with nontruly passive dynamics and that the resulting closed-loop systems possess a well-defined Lyapunov energy function with a clear physical interpretation.

(1) the interconnection and damping passivity-based control framework is applicable to power system stabilization; (2) the presence of resistive elements necessitates the introduction of state modulated interconnections; (3) the total energy function of the closed-loop system has a well-defined physical meaning; and (4) the closed-loop system is robust to small changes in the system parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of designing a nonlinear static feedback law that ensures asymptotic stabilization of the n-generator power system with nonnegligable transfer conductances.

the development of a new methodology for the transient stabilization of multimachines power systems and with the design of a nonlinear static control law that ensures asymptotic stabilization with a well-defined domain of attraction.
the stabilization of a complex nonlinear dynamical system with nonnegligibly large resistive elements and with a well-defined Lyapunov-like function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is able to stabilize multimachine power systems in a transient fashion with a Lyapunov estimate of the domain-of-attraction size.

the interconnection and damping passivity-based control method can be successfully applied to the stabilization of multimachine synchronous generator systems with nontrigid transmission lines and loads.
we have developed a methodology that allows us to design a stabilizing feedback law that is robust to the presence of lossy transmission lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a systematic procedure for the design of a nonlinear static feedback law for multimachine power systems that ensures asymptotic stabilization of the desired operating point and that the closed-loop system is port-controlled Hamiltonian with a bona fide total energy function.
we are able to stabilize a multimachine power system with nontrivial interconnection resistances by means of an interconnection and damping-assignment passivity-based control law.
we are able to stabilize the system with the full set of parameters, and that the control law we design is a nonlinear static feedback of the generator excitation fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the nonpassivity of the system, a nonlinear feedback law can be designed that renders the closed-loop system passivity-dissipative with respect to the total energy function and, hence, asymptotically stable.
the interconnection and damping passivity-based control framework can be successfully applied to the design of nonlinear feedback laws for the stabilization of large-scale power systems.
the interconnection and damping passivity-based control approach is applicable to a much wider range of power systems than the existing literature would suggest.
